verdict_reason: Both attributed kernels are exact. Self-BLEU: BLME's _self_bleu_single is bit-identical to Texygen's calc_bleu (nltk sentence_bleu, uniform (1/4,)*4 weights, SmoothingFunction().method1) -- worst absolute difference 0.000e+00 over 4,000 randomised hypothesis/reference cases. Distinct-n: the collection-level union-of-types over total generated tokens matches an independent re-derivation to 0.000e+00 over 6,000 checks, and the degenerate case is handled the way Li et al. define it (ten duplicate [1,2] completions give corpus Distinct-1 = 0.1 with the per-completion mean of 1.0 kept under its own separate name).
comparable_reason: Distinct-n is a per-TOKEN ratio, so a tokenizer that splits more finely produces more tokens for the same text and a different denominator; the metric is therefore only comparable within a tokenizer family without a per-character or per-word renormalisation, and none is emitted. Self-BLEU is comparable but depends strongly on the size of the reference collection: measured on the released Texygen MLE corpus it rises 0.287690813 (N=400) -> 0.369847573 (N=1000) -> 0.432013278 (N=2000) -> 0.491091064 (N=4000) toward the published 0.583 at N=9984, so two runs with different completion counts are not on the same scale. The shipped config produces 48 completions per model. The sampling_entropy_* family is of the TEMPERED (temperature 0.8) distribution, which the key name says.
github_reason: Ran the released Texygen kernel (nltk sentence_bleu with method1 smoothing and uniform 4-gram weights, which is exactly what Texygen's SelfBleu.calc_bleu calls) head-to-head with BLME's _self_bleu_single on 4,000 randomised cases: worst absolute difference 0.000e+00. I also ran BLME's leave-one-out collection statistic on the authors' own released docs/instances/mle.txt.
paper_reason: Texygen (Zhu et al. 2018) Table 3 publishes MLE Self-BLEU-4 = 0.583 on the corpus released as docs/instances/mle.txt (9,984 sentences). The statistic is leave-one-out over the whole collection and is O(N^2) in nltk, so I evaluated prefixes rather than the full corpus: BLME returns 0.287690813 at N=400, 0.369847573 at N=1000, 0.432013278 at N=2000 and 0.491091064 at N=4000 -- monotonically increasing toward 0.583 as the reference set grows, exactly the expected behaviour, and 84.2% of the published value at 40% of the corpus. I did not reach N=9984 and therefore do not claim a relative error against 0.583. The KERNEL is exact (0.000e+00 against the released Texygen/nltk call over 4,000 cases); it is the population size I did not complete.
confounds_reason: Distinct-n's denominator is the generated TOKEN count, so tokenizer granularity enters directly and vocabulary size is the architectural parameter to watch; I did not run the generation panel across models (generation at the study config is the most expensive task in the batch and I prioritised the fidelity checks), so I report the mechanism rather than a measured correlation. Self-BLEU has no width or depth term but does depend on completion count, which is fixed at 48 by the config in every run.
defects: CODE / GLOBAL RNG NOT RESTORED (measured): generation_diversity.py:232-239 calls torch.manual_seed(seed) and never restores the caller's state. Starting from seed 999, running the task changed 2,495 of 5,056 CPU RNG state bytes, and the next five torch.randn draws went from [-0.837879, 0.456360, 0.348142, -0.137128, 0.220171] to [1.704765, -0.228016, -0.119197, 1.899779, -1.435209]. Any co-resident task that draws from the global torch RNG therefore depends on whether this one ran first. Wrap in torch.random.fork_rng().

CODE / ENTROPY POSITION MISALIGNMENT: _trim_completion (generation_diversity.py:93-104) DROPS interior pad tokens, but the entropy summaries at :336-345 select the first len(trimmed) RAW generation steps. Demonstrated: _trim_completion([5,1,7,2,9], eos=2, pad=1) returns [5,7], whose raw positions are [0,2], while the code reads per_token_H[row, :2] = positions [0,1] -- it uses the entropy of the dropped pad step and omits the retained one. Reachability: the drop branch requires pad_token_id != eos_token_id, which holds for EleutherAI/pythia-70m (eos=0, pad=1) and facebook/opt-125m (eos=2, pad=1), both in the study zoo, and top_k is pinned to 0 so every vocabulary item including the pad id has nonzero sampling probability. Rare, but not structurally impossible. Index by the RETAINED positions.

CONFIG / KEY NAME MISMATCH: the study override at beyond_benchmarks/configs/tasks.yaml:252 sets n_samples: 8, but the task reads n_samples_per_prompt (generation_diversity.py:201) and the merged defaults.yaml:306 supplies 6. The override is silently inert; num_prompts: 10 also exceeds the built-in bank of 8 prompts, so runs execute 8 prompts x 6 samples = 48 completions rather than the apparent 80.

PROTOCOL: temperature is 0.8 by default, so sampling_entropy_first_q / _last_q / _collapse_delta are entropies of the TEMPERED sampling distribution, not the model's own next-token distribution. The key prefix says 'sampling', which is honest, but the difference should be stated wherever the number is interpreted.

DOC/PROVENANCE: the module docstring at :5-17 and task_metadata.py:118 still describe per-completion Distinct-n and same-prompt Self-BLEU, both of which were changed to collection scope; on ten duplicate [1,2] completions the two scopes give 0.1 and 1.0.
fix: Restore the caller's RNG (torch.random.fork_rng() around the generation loop). Index per-token entropies by the RETAINED generation positions rather than by a prefix of length len(trimmed). Rename the study override key to n_samples_per_prompt, and either extend the prompt bank to 10 or clamp num_prompts with a warning.
